subject.title: [RFC] Multi-Agent Collaboration Enhancement: Capability Profiling + Shared Blackboard + Layered Memory + Token Cost Governance

question: Should OpenClaw pursue this four-layer multi-agent collaboration stack in core, and if so which narrow first phase owns storage, visibility, and budget policy?
rationale: The request conflicts with current lean-core and heavy-orchestration guardrails unless maintainers intentionally choose a staged core design or plugin/API path.

options.title: Approve a narrow core first phase
options.body: Define one initial primitive, such as capability/performance records or a meeting/handoff on-ramp, with SQLite storage, visibility rules, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep it outside core for now
options.body: Use plugins, ClawHub, or missing API seams for optional orchestration while preserving the existing lean core runtime.

options.title: Split and close the umbrella later
options.body: Convert the RFC into smaller canonical issues for profile storage, blackboard semantics, memory visibility, and budget governance, then close the umbrella when those owners exist.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core first phase
recommendation.body: Define one initial primitive, such as capability/performance records or a meeting/handoff on-ramp, with SQLite storage, visibility rules, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner is the strongest current-history signal for subagent runtime seams and related multi-agent scoping discussions.
